title: Hodge Decomposition: Type and Symmetry
mathematical_role: Represent Hodge decomposition schematically in bidegree without inventing Hodge numbers, showing conjugation symmetry and the (p,p) diagonal relevant to algebraic-cycle classes.
learning_objective: Interpret H^k(X,C) as a direct sum of H^(p,q), identify complex-conjugate bidegrees, and understand that algebraic-cycle classes lie on the (p,p) diagonal without concluding that every rational diagonal class is algebraic.
literal_semantics: For compact Kahler manifolds, H^k(X,C) decomposes as the direct sum of H^(p,q)(X) over p+q=k.
Complex conjugation exchanges H^(p,q) and H^(q,p).
Algebraic cycle classes have Hodge type (p,p).
For smooth projective complex varieties, rational (p,p) type is necessary for a rational class to be algebraic, but general sufficiency is the Hodge conjecture.
nonliteral_semantics: The schematic diamond assigns no numerical Hodge numbers to any particular variety.
Box size and geometric distance do not encode dimensions of Hodge summands.
The central (p,p) box is not asserted to consist entirely of algebraic classes.

notes: Candidate semantics are bounded by the existing documentary source; no new mathematical source is admitted by this visual operation.

accessibility.alt_text: A schematic Hodge bidegree diamond shows the direct-sum decomposition, conjugation between p,q and q,p, and a labelled p,p diagonal box, with text saying no Hodge numbers are assigned and p,p type does not prove algebraicity.
accessibility.long_description: A formula panel states the Hodge direct-sum decomposition and complex-conjugation symmetry. The central schematic diamond labels a conjugate pair H^(p,q) and H^(q,p) and a diagonal H^(p,p) component. A lower guardrail states that algebraic-cycle classes occur on the diagonal but that a rational p,p class is not known to be algebraic in general.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: The plate faithfully depicts the structural Hodge decomposition and conjugation symmetry while preserving the open algebraicity boundary.
not_claimed: Specific Hodge numbers for a chosen variety
That every rational (p,p) class is algebraic

supersession_reason: Replace an unlabeled ornamental diamond with a bidegree-schematic decomposition that explicitly marks symmetry, diagonal type, and the algebraicity boundary.
